transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortiz (Redwood SE), Samantha Reed (CISO - Clearwater), Tom Baxter (Head of Infrastructure), Priya Nair (Compliance Manager)

Summary: Quick posture review of Redwood's SOC 2 / ISO 27001 artifacts, access to Trust Center, and controls mapping. Technical questions about KMS/BYOK, private VPC deployment, audit logs, RBAC/SSO integration, and data residency requirements.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. Myself, Maya Chen, AE for Redwood Inference; with me is Lucas Ortiz, our SE who will cover the technical parts.
00:18 Samantha Reed: Hi Maya, hi Lucas, thanks. We're Samantha (CISO), Tom (infra), Priya (compliance). We put this meeting to make sure we understand the reports and how Redwood maps to our SOC 2 controls.
00:32 Maya Chen: Great, can we confirm the objectives? We'll walk through the redacted SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert scope, show where the Trust Center lives, and then Lucas will cover VPC/private deploy and KMS options. Any other asks?
00:48 Priya Nair: Please focus on encryption key management, audit logs retention and whether we can export logs to our SIEM. Also RBAC and SSO provisioning.
01:05 Lucas Ortiz: Absolutely. Quick note on naming, sometimes our docs say "Redwood Private" or "Redwood Dedication" in older decks, sorry for the inconsistency.
01:22 Tom Baxter: No problem, just want to make sure features map to our procurement needs. Timelinewise we have legal review starting mid-May.
01:35 Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll circle back on artifacts.

02:10 Topics - SOC 2 / ISO artifacts
02:22 Maya Chen: We have a redacted SOC 2 Type II report covering the period Oct 2024 - Mar 2026; we'll share a redacted version. We also have ISO 27001 certificate - scope includes hosted and VPC private deployments in our cloud regions.
02:45 Samantha Reed: For redaction, can you confirm you remove customer names and sample data but keep control descriptions and tests? We need evidence mapping.
02:58 Maya Chen: Yes, redacted report will preserve control narratives and testing outcomes. It won't have customer PII.
03:14 Priya Nair: Do you have a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps CC controls to Redwood controls?
03:27 Lucas Ortiz: Yes - we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet in the Trust Center. We'll provide a copy and can annotate with how each control is implemented in the platform.
03:40 Samantha Reed: How much access do we get to the Trust Center? Read-only or we get a shared link?
03:48 Maya Chen: We'll send a shareable Trust Center link for Clearwater's security team; it's read-only but contains the latest artifacts and the mapping doc. We'll also attach the specific evidence bundles for SOC 2 tests where possible.

06:05 Topics - RBAC & SSO
06:12 Tom Baxter: On RBAC, does Redwood support fine-grained roles? We need to limit access to model management and billing separately.
06:28 Lucas Ortiz: Yes, RBAC supports role-based permissions; out-of-the-box roles, and custom roles via the Console. For SSO we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. There's a small caveat around API keys for service accounts - recommended pattern is scoped API keys with limited permissions.
06:55 Samantha Reed: Do you support enforced MFA for admin accounts and can we integrate with our IdP?
07:04 Maya Chen: Enforced MFA is supported via SSO when you set it up in your IdP. We also support session timeout policies and audit of admin actions.

09:30 Topics - Audit logs
09:40 Priya Nair: What does audit logging look like? Retention, export, and tamper evidence?
09:48 Lucas Ortiz: Audit logs include admin console events, model deployment events, API key creation, and failed auth attempts. Logs are stored for 12 months by default in hosted plans; for Dedicated/Private deployments retention can be configured. We can export logs to your SIEM via push or S3 export. Tamper evidence is provided via append-only storage and checksums.
10:15 Samantha Reed: Can we get a quick example log schema?
10:21 Lucas Ortiz: Yes, we'll attach a sample log extract in the Trust Center; note sometimes field names in the export are abbreviated - in earlier exports we had 'evt_type' and 'usr_id' which some teams found confusing.

13:05 Topics - Data residency / Private deployment
13:13 Tom Baxter: We have a EU residency requirement for PHI-adjacent metadata; would Redwood host in eu-west region or do we need Private?
13:22 Maya Chen: We support regional deployments; for strict residency you can use Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with pinned region. For on-prem options, we provide an on-prem package but that's a larger engagement.
13:45 Tom Baxter: If we go VPC Private, how does network connectivity work? VPC peering, PrivateLink?
13:54 Lucas Ortiz: We support VPC peering and private endpoints; the Private deployment is customer-managed VPC with a control plane access pattern. We'll provide diagrams in the runbook. Note - sometimes our doc says 'KV cache' and gets transcribed as 'K-V cash' in notes, ignore that.

17:00 Topics - Encryption / KMS / BYOK
17:12 Priya Nair: Key management - is BYOK supported? Can keys be rotated and do you use HSMs?
17:24 Lucas Ortiz: We support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (BYOK) via your KMS or HSM. For cloud KMS we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS; we also have an HSM-backed option for Dedicated/Private. Key rotation policies are supported, and we can provide key rotation logs. There is a short lead time for HSM provisioning on private deployments.
17:56 Samantha Reed: What about encryption at rest for cached KV and for model artifacts?
18:05 Lucas Ortiz: Everything at rest is AES-256. KV cache is encrypted; model artifacts in object storage are encrypted at rest. In transit we use TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers.

22:30 Customer concerns / imperfect transcription
22:38 Samantha Reed: A common ask is whether audit logs can be routed to our SIEM with guaranteed delivery. You said S3 push; do you support Kinesis or pub/sub?
22:48 Lucas Ortiz: We support S3 export and direct SIEM integration via syslog or HTTP push. For high-volume streaming we recommend a Kinesis pipeline on the customer side; Redwood can push to a customer-owned S3 bucket and lifecycle rules apply.

26:10 Technical deep-dive points
26:20 Tom Baxter: On Private deployment, what's the support SLA and who manages OS patching?
26:29 Maya Chen: For Private, maintenance responsibilities are defined in the SOW. For a hosted Private we can manage the runtime patching as part of the Dedicated offering; for fully customer-managed on-prem, we provide an ops bundle but the customer owns OS patching.
26:50 Tom Baxter: Ok, we'll flag which model of Private we want in the SOW.

31:00 Compliance evidence & controls mapping
31:12 Priya Nair: For controls mapping, can you map Redwood controls to our SOC 2 controls (CC6, CC7 etc.)?
31:20 Lucas Ortiz: Yes we'll provide a mapping sheet. Note that some of our control IDs don't line up one-to-one with your control numbers, we'll add commentary.
31:35 Samantha Reed: Will you include sample test evidence for change control and incident response?
31:43 Maya Chen: We'll include sample evidence for change management, incident response timelines, and penetration test high-level results. Full pentest reports are redacted but findings summary will be included.

38:00 Procurement & timeline
38:15 Maya Chen: You mentioned legal starts mid-May - we'll prioritize the SOC/ISO artifacts to meet that. Pricing/contract questions should go through your procurement, we can loop legal.
38:30 Tom Baxter: For the pilot, we want a 6-week PoC with dedicated capacity in eu-west and KMS BYOK. Is that feasible?
38:40 Lucas Ortiz: Feasible, subject to capacity and SOW. We can provision dedicated pool and BYOK keys; HSM lead times may extend the schedule.

44:10 Clarifying small points
44:22 Samantha Reed: One quick question on session management: can we set session length to 30 min for admins?
44:30 Maya Chen: Yes via SSO policy on your IdP and our session settings. We'll add recommended settings in the runbook.

49:00 Recap & next steps
49:10 Maya Chen: Recap - Redwood to send: redacted SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, Trust Center link, controls mapping spreadsheet, sample audit log extract, and VPC/KMS runbook. Lucas will lead the technical runbook. Customer to confirm residency and regulated datasets. We'll schedule the KMS deep dive the week of May 4.
49:40 Samantha Reed: Sounds good. Priya will compile controls questions and send them back.
49:50 Priya Nair: Yep, I'll send a prioritized list.
50:00 Tom Baxter: We'll follow up on procurement and legal and share timelines.

52:10 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone; I will share artifacts by Friday. Lucas and I will set up the KMS deep-dive.
52:20 Samantha Reed: Thanks, bye.
52:25 Tom Baxter: Thanks.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-attribution and abbreviation in transcripts (e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedication, KV cache -> K-V cash). There are filler words and short interruptions.

End of transcript.
